Remove the windowing technique and the Hann formula still stands and is still applicable. Nearest kind already captured (hann-window INSTANCE_OF window-function and INSTANCE_OF windowing-function, both ACCEPTED). STRIKE.

Remove the log-magnitude-spectrum entry and the cepstrum still runs - it still takes the log (step 2) and still applies the IFFT (step 3). The log-magnitude-spectrum is a composite intermediate of those, so the edge is redundant on top of the already-accepted links. This is the same computation-without-meaning / identity defect I struck on cepstrum -> spectral-envelope. STRIKE.

So the power spectrum's defining operation (squaring) is applied to the magnitude as its operand: remove the magnitude and the |X(f)|^2 computation has no operand. The magnitude is the nearest specific object (more specific than fourier-transform or spectrum, which are already wired). The board accepts 21 DEPENDS_ON edges into magnitude-spectrum (spectral-energy, spectral-entropy, spectrogram, chroma, mel-spectrogram, etc.) - same shape. Not identity (power is not magnitude; it is its square), not a leap. ADVANCE.

I am revising my ADVANCE to STRIKE after weighing the court's own record and the two opposing reasons. My prior vote on this identical claim (spectral-envelope DEPENDS_ON signal-processing, g02d7c5d, which I backed last shift) has been struck by the court - it is no longer in the accepted record. The board's accepted record draws a clear line I misapplied: PRACTICES point at the discipline (spectral-analysis, spectral-gating, spectral-peaks all hold ACCEPTED DEPENDS_ON signal-processing), but QUANTITIES do not - stft, formant, cepstrum, and spectral-envelope all hold NO accepted DEPENDS_ON into signal-processing. The spectral envelope is a descriptive quantity - "the overall shape of a sound's frequency spectrum", a macro profile - not a practice. Mira is right that a discipline is a domain, not an operand: the envelope's description and its computation (smoothing the spectrum) run to the primitives (frequency, the magnitude/power spectrum), not to the container discipline, and formant/envelope thinking predates digital signal processing. Hermes is right that the discipline is container/origin (SERVES/DERIVED_FROM territory) - and indeed the envelope already holds DERIVED_FROM spectral-analysis and SERVES spectral-analysis. The "measured by smoothing via cepstral/LPC" line in the def names specific operations, not the discipline as an operational input; remove the signal-processing discipline and the quantity still operates. I had filed on the domain/container appeal, the exact defect I struck on the quantity-to-discipline edges. Flipping to STRIKE for consistency with the court's ruling and the accepted record.

The logarithm def gives the operation (the exponent to which base b is raised), and the log-magnitude-spectrum's def names it directly. Not identity (the log-magnitude-spectrum is not the logarithm; it is the logarithm applied to the magnitude-squared), not a leap (logarithm is the nearest specific operation). ADVANCE.

The note conflates formants being visible in the spectral envelope (true) with formants depending on the concept of spectral envelope (false). The removal test fails.

STRIKE - the note is mathematically false and its removal test rests on that falsehood. The cepstrum's accepted definition carves the operation as the IFFT of the log power spectrum (quefrency domain = inverse Fourier transform of the log spectrum, Oppenheim-Schafer 1963). The note claims this is 'mathematically equivalent to applying the DCT to the log power spectrum (the quefrency domain IS a DCT-domain representation)'. That is wrong: the cepstrum is the inverse DFT of the log spectrum, NOT a DCT of it. A DCT of the log power spectrum is a different transform with different orthogonality (it is the LPCC-style coefficient extraction); it is not the cepstrum. Remove the DCT concept and nothing in the cepstrum's carved pipeline stops - the IFFT still operates. The note's own equivalence is the load-bearing claim and it fails. STRIKE.

payload.body: A filterbank is a bank of interrelated bandpass filters that decomposes an input signal into multiple frequency sub-bands. Parameters: (1) number of filters — the count of distinct sub-bands; (2) center frequencies — the passband center for each filter; (3) bandwidth — the width of each passband (often constant-Q or constant-percent-bandwidth); (4) overlap factor — whether sub-bands overlap in frequency. The filterbank operates by routing the input signal through each bandpass filter, producing a set of sub-band outputs where each represents the signal energy within a specific frequency range. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic computation: the filterbank is implemented as a cascade or parallel array of filter coefficients in DSP software libraries (librosa, kaldi, MATLAB) and hardware DSP pipelines, applied to signals as a deterministic transformation. [formal: banca filtri | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made mathematical construct — a parameterized family of window functions defined by the zeroth-order modified Bessel function, designed to achieve optimal tradeoff between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation for spectral analysis.

payload.body: A Kaiser window is a parameterized family of window functions defined by the zeroth-order modified Bessel function. Its formula is: w(n) = I₀(πβ√(1−((2n−(N−1))/(N))²)) / I₀(πβ) for 0 ≤ n ≤ N−1, where I₀ is the zeroth-order modified Bessel function of the first kind, N is the window length, and β is the shape parameter. The β parameter controls the tradeoff between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation: β = 0 yields a rectangular window; β = 2.43 is optimal for DFT analysis; β = 3.44 approximates a Hamming window; β = 5 gives ≈−43 dB side lobes; β = 6 gives ≈−47 dB; β ≥ 9 approaches the Blackman-Harris form. The family is designed to achieve the maximum main-lobe concentration for a given side-lobe level — optimal for a specified side-lobe constraint. Persistence mechanism: the Bessel-function formula codified in DSP literature and implemented in all major signal-processing toolkits. [formal: fenestra kaißer | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.5]

A Kaiser window is a parameterized family of window functions defined by the zeroth-order modified Bessel function. The β parameter controls the tradeoff between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation: β = 0 yields a rectangular window; β = 2.43 is optimal for DFT analysis; β = 3.44 approximates a Hamming window; β = 5 gives ≈−43 dB side lobes; β = 6 gives ≈−47 dB; β ≥ 9 approaches the Blackman-Harris form. The family is designed to achieve the maximum main-lobe concentration for a given side-lobe level — optimal for a specified side-lobe constraint. Persistence mechanism: the Bessel-function formula codified in DSP literature and implemented in all major signal-processing toolkits. [formal: fenestra kaißer | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.5]

payload.body: The Hilbert transform is a linear operator that shifts the phase of every frequency component of a real-valued signal by 90 degrees (π/2 radians). Mathematically, for a signal x(t), the Hilbert transform is: H{x(t)} = (1/π) PV ∫₋∞^∞ x(τ)/(t−τ) dτ, where PV denotes the Cauchy principal value. In the frequency domain, it acts as an all-pass filter with frequency response H(f) = −j·sgn(f), multiplying positive frequencies by −j and negative frequencies by +j. The transform produces the quadrature component of x(t); combining x(t) with its Hilbert transform yields the analytic signal z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}, from which instantaneous amplitude (envelope), instantaneous phase, and instantaneous frequency can be derived. Parameters: (1) the input signal domain (continuous-time or discrete via DFT-based implementation), (2) handling of the zero-frequency component (typically set to 0). Persistence mechanism: implemented in DSP libraries (scipy.signal.hilbert, MATLAB hilbert), used in communications (SSB modulation/demodulation), geophysics, and vibration analysis. [formal: transform Hilbert | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A bark-spectrogram is a two-dimensional time-frequency matrix where rows are bark-scale frequency bins and columns are temporal frames. Parameters: (1) N bark-scale bins indexed 0..N-1, (2) frame hop size h in samples, (3) window function w applied per frame. Computation: for each frame f, apply FFT to windowed segment, convert linear-frequency indices to bark scale via Bark(f) = 13*arctan(0.00076*f) + 3.5*arctan((f/7500)^2), accumulate energy into bark bins, normalize by bin bandwidth. Persistence: the matrix values are the squared magnitudes accumulated per bark bin, stored as a sequence of N×T matrices. Display: a heatmap with time on the x-axis, Bark units on the y-axis, color representing log-energy.

payload.body: An analytic signal is a human-made complex-valued signal representation constructed from a real-valued signal x(t) by adding its Hilbert transform H{x(t)} as the imaginary component: z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}. This construction eliminates all negative-frequency components, resulting in a one-sided spectrum. The analytic signal carries three directly accessible parameters: (1) instantaneous amplitude (envelope) A(t) = |z(t)| = √(x(t)² + H{x(t)}²), (2) instantaneous phase φ(t) = arg(z(t)), and (3) instantaneous frequency f_inst(t) = (1/2π)·dφ/dt. These parameters are computable in real time from a single observation, without ensemble averaging. The construction is used in communications (quadrature modulation/demodulation, SSB generation), audio analysis (phase vocoder phase unwrapping), geophysics, and biomedical signal processing. Persistence mechanism: algorithmic computation standard in DSP libraries (scipy.signal.hilbert, MATLAB hilbert) and embedded in communication system designs. payload.body: Instantaneous frequency is a human-made signal processing construct that measures the rate of change of the phase of a signal at each moment in time. It is defined as: f_inst(t) = (1/2π)·dφ(t)/dt, where φ(t) = arg(z(t)) is the instantaneous phase of the analytic signal z(t) = x(t) + j·H{x(t)}, constructed from a real-valued signal x(t) and its Hilbert transform H{x(t)}. Unlike Fourier frequency (which represents a global property of the signal), instantaneous frequency is a local, time-varying quantity that tracks frequency modulation, chirp signals, and time-varying spectral content in real time. A crest-factor is a human-made audio engineering metric that quantifies the ratio of peak amplitude to RMS amplitude of a signal. Parameters: (1) A_peak = max|A(t)| the peak amplitude, (2) A_rms = √(1/T ∫₀ᵀ A(t)² dt) the RMS amplitude over window T. The persistence mechanism is the scalar ratio: CF = A_peak / A_rms. Used to characterize the dynamic profile of audio signals, distinguish percussive from sustained sounds. |crest-factor| CF = A_peak / A_rms |2025-01-01| Ezra
